acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: Fourteen tools/history actions reuse Rust input and action layout/scene recipes in contiguous Metal groups; tools dismiss reuses the Rust close-control recipe. Native services, confirmations, IME, focus and AX remain adapters.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

additional_performance_scenario_coverage.purpose: Execute all four opt-in performance scenarios as additional automated coverage, with their default 30 trials. Metal validation is enabled; these are not controlled CPU/GPU/drawable presentation comparisons.

contracts: Five Time Machine, four shortcut, three provider and two history actions use shared Rust pointer/key input, button/group geometry and primitives. Contiguous body actions batch into 4/1/1 groups across the first three pages; history clear/more use two standalone groups. The header close has its own existing dismiss recipe/canvas. Native Button/focus/AX/event adapters remain.

Views retains the original native button hierarchy. The Rust branch has childless scene buttons with no native MdTextButton labels. Native generation/workspace/profile checks still gate deferred tools commands; IME, validation, confirmations and service mutations remain unchanged.

An action child that leaves the viewport cancels its pressed state even when other children keep the shared group visible. Rebuild/profile/workspace and widget hide cancel input; native scrolling synchronizes the grouped GPU clips.

History busy labels dispatch through the native/scene button adapter. Rebuilding history during an active operation now preserves the disabled Czyszczenie… label on both backends. Hiding the standalone More control also hides its scene group so an empty layout gap does not remain.

New real Cocoa Space coverage saves a Unicode snapshot, saves/selects/defaults/deletes a provider and dismisses the tools panel. Busy/rebuild tests verify dynamic labels and disabled state. The existing real 205-row history scenario now scrolls after successful presentation and uses Space to load beyond the first 200 rows, retaining its stale-result and profile assertions.

Dedicated Metal coverage checks all fourteen action adapters, childless controls, 4/1/1/2 batching, scene text and clipped screen bounds. A fixture-only trailing spacer establishes partial-group scrolling and verifies cancellation of a fully clipped pressed child while the group remains visible; hide/rebuild and close-canvas visibility are checked.
Close artwork uses the existing analytic Rust dismiss symbol; pixel-identical native vector paths are not claimed. No new crate/library/dependency or license is introduced.
limits: Tools headers/explanatory/status copy, form/controller coordination and result lists remain native. Other forms, browser-service panels, preference UI descriptions/data and remaining busy/status coordination, outer layout and native interaction/container ownership remain open.
Native popup/manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, complex bidi/RTL, pointer/trackpad, scale/theme, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
Optional scenarios provide execution coverage; no controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup comparison is claimed.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.
initial_compile_issue: Two ASSERT_NO_FATAL_FAILURE macros on one source line generated duplicate gtest labels. They now occupy separate lines; runtime assertions and production code were unchanged by that fix.

input.note: The new Cocoa snapshot/provider flow did not observe a snapshot on either backend. All other common and GPU cases passed. The revised fixture explicitly selects the work workspace before opening tools and includes failed-flow diagnostics; the production code and success assertions are unchanged.

Explicit workspace context did not fix the assertion. Both backends reported before=0 after=2, rebuilt=true and success UI. WorkspaceWindow::ScheduleSessionSave also saves an automatic restore point. Final acceptance counts exactly one snapshot with the requested unique title, preserving real Cocoa button activation.

probe_resolution: The new Cocoa save test initially expected the total snapshot count to grow by exactly one. Both backends also created an automatic restore point via ScheduleSessionSave. The second probe reported before=0 after=2, rebuilt=true and success UI. Final acceptance verifies exactly one newly named snapshot and its nonempty ID, including after subsequent provider operations. Production code was unchanged between these probes.

input.note: Unchanged isolated Views run reproduced the presentation wait failure at provider Save. Final test waits for compositor visibility/size and focuses/invalidates actual contents before requesting successful presentation; the successful-presentation requirement and all domain assertions remain.

presentation_probe.resolution: After the snapshot assertion fix, Metal passed all critical cases. Views then hit a successful-presentation wait before provider Save; an unchanged isolated run reproduced it. The final test focuses the actual button, waits for a visible nonempty compositor and invalidates the real contents before requesting successful presentation. The physical-success requirement and all operation assertions remain; a platform-level root cause is not fully established.
